descriptions.text: Kame's aggregation router (0x14bb98...4d80) on Sei exposed a swap(SwapParams) function that performed an arbitrary external call to an attacker-controlled executor address with attacker-controlled executeParams calldata, all under the router's own context. Because the router itself held token approvals from users, the attacker set executor to the USDC token address and executeParams to an encoded transferFrom(targetUser, attacker, fullBalance) call. The router dutifully executed it, pulling the victim's entire approved USDC balance via the router's allowance. There was no allow-listing of call targets/selectors or validation that the external call wasn't a token transferFrom abusing user approvals, resulting in ~18,167 USD stolen. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://seiscan.io//tx/0x6150ec6b2b1b46d1bcba0cab9c3a77b5bca218fd1cdaad1ddc7a916e4ce792ec Analysis: https://x.com/SupremacyHQ/status/1966909841483636849

Kame Aggregator suffered an exploit due to a design flaw in the swap() function, which allowed arbitrary executor calls. This vulnerability enabled attackers to transfer tokens authorized to the AggregationRouter by users, particularly those with unlimited or oversized approvals. The total value of affected assets was approximately $1.32 million, of which around $946,000 was recovered by the Kame team from the primary exploiter, and about $22,000 was recovered by white-hat hackers.

On 12 September 2025, Kame Aggregator on Sei was exploited for approximately $1.3M. Attackers abused a swap logic flaw in the AggregationRouter contract, using malicious executor contracts to drain user-approved tokens. Partial recovery (185 ETH) occurred, but most losses remain unrecovered. The AggregationRouter swap() function accepted arbitrary executor addresses from user input, allowing attacker-controlled contracts to execute unvalidated external calls. This enabled draining of user token approvals with no whitelist or parameter checks.
